examShortTricks: Trick 1: Fantasy questions test SUSPENSION OF DISBELIEF — explain how the writer makes impossible events feel real (consistent rules, vivid detail, relatable characters).
Trick 2: Symbol questions: fantasy objects usually symbolise real desires or fears — name the symbol and its real-world meaning.
Trick 3: 'Why do readers enjoy fantasy?' — answer with escapism PLUS insight: fantasy tells truths about reality through the impossible.
practiceQuestions: Q. What makes a fantasy story believable? (2 marks) — internal consistency of the imagined world and characters with real emotions.
Q. What might a magical object in the story symbolise? (2 marks) — a real human wish or fear; justify from the plot.
keyPoints: Fantasy is not escape only — it mirrors real fears and desires symbolically.
Identify the 'impossible' element and explain its realistic meaning.
